title: Baked pears with walnuts and honey

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Pears, walnuts, honey, butter, an orange, cinnamon and Greek yoghurt are all plain kitchen staples with no factory-made products.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream supermarket, and 50g of walnuts is not a treat purchase.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a baking dish, a small bowl, a knife and an oven, and halving and coring pears is beginner technique.

works.reason: Eight pear halves with a walnut, honey and butter filling, baked at 190°C for 25 to 30 minutes with juice and water, gives a sensible snack for four with enough liquid for pan juices.

honest_times.reason: Ten minutes covers halving and coring four pears, chopping walnuts, zesting and juicing an orange and mixing, and the 30 minutes of cook time matches the bake.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon appear in the steps, nothing unlisted is used apart from water, and each name matches its id.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm baked stored pears suit a cold January afternoon, and the pears are clearly the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, nuts and yoghurt make a satisfying snack of real food, with only modest honey.
